topic: What payload transponder allocation strategies balance spectral efficiency with dynamic QoS demands from ML traffic classification?
consensus_response: To balance spectral efficiency with dynamic QoS demands from ML traffic classification, payload transponder allocation strategies should integrate Adaptive Modulation and Coding (AMC) techniques with Edge Computing and Federated Learning. This approach enables real-time processing and analysis of traffic data for more accurate QoS adaptation and spectral efficiency optimization. By considering the interaction between layer 3 and layer 2, qos mechanisms can work jointly together to enable effective qos management. Machine learning-based solutions can classify internet traffic into predefined categories and determine the actual demands of a flow in terms of necessary bandwidth, maximum loss, latency, and jitter.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the limitations of current payload transponder allocation strategies, including DVB-S2/RCS2, WiBACK, and QoS-OSPF with RSVP approaches. These methods have trade-offs in spectral efficiency and qos adaptation due to fixed latency on satellite links and limited consideration of other parameters like latency or jitter.
